events.what: No CEO or CFO change since 2025-04-01. Own 8-K Item 5.02 query (2024-07-01 to 2026-10-02) returned only the 2024 board filing; Items 2.01/1.01 none. Baba 'first earnings call / since joining' check: CFO Bill Wheat on every call back to at least FY2021 (document_id 76850, 41398)

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update found in corpus; guidance is quarterly (home sales gross margin and pre-tax margin ranges).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Management guides home sales gross margin and consolidated pre-tax margin one quarter ahead (Q4 FY2026: 20.5% to 21% gross, 12.3% to 12.8% pre-tax) and frames the outlook as 'relatively stable'. There is no expansion target, level with a year, or peer gap. Margin is set by incentives and mortgage rate buydowns (the housing cycle), not by a self-help program. Fiscal year ends September; Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years.

street.gap_assumption: No management target, so no gap. Fiscal year ends September; Baba FY = company fiscal year. Street path continues to 14.55% FY2029 and 15.07% FY2030. D is scored on the no-level rule (4-month revision -2.4%), but the 12-month revision is -20.7%, so estimates only just stopped falling.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q2 FY2026, Q3 FY2026], EBITDA / revenue from consensus actuals: Q2 828.1/7,558.1 = 11.0% vs 1,026.1/7,734.0 = 13.3%; Q3 1,184.0/9,227.1 = 12.8% vs 1,290.1/9,225.7 = 14.0%. Q3 home sales gross margin 20.7% beat the guide on lower stick and brick costs and slightly lower incentives (Hansen, document_id 41398). FY2026 closings guide cut to 83,800 to 84,300.

disqualifier_reason: Catalyst older than 18 months with no pending change: the internal CEO succession was effective 2023-10-01 (36 months ago), and the last board additions were 2024-08-26. There is no CFO change, no acquisition and no Investor Day. Margin is also cycle-driven (incentives and mortgage rates), close to the commodity-driven exclusion. EBITDA margin (12.4% forward) is above the industry median (9.6%), so this is not a below-peer margin story.
verdict: Not a GXO setup: no leadership change or deal in the window, no margin target, cycle-driven margins already above the industry median, and only A (down 29%) and the mechanical D score.
open_questions: Does the Q4 FY2026 call (late October) give a fiscal 2027 gross margin outlook, the first annual framing?
How much of FY2029 consensus margin expansion (14.55%) depends on lower mortgage rates rather than anything D.R. Horton controls?
Is there any pending succession at CFO (Wheat, born 1966) or COO that could create a catalyst?
